newsitem.title: UK: Copper price hits 1-year high, tests resistance.
newsitem.headline: Copper price hits 1-year high, tests resistance.

text.p: A stronger fundamental and technical picture helped lift the price of London Metal Exchange (LME) copper to the highest for a year at $2,550 per tonne on Wednesday.
Several traders said the market will forge further ahead if it can overcome technicals resistance at this level.
Copper had closed the afternoon LME kerb on Tuesday at $2,514 while the traders pegged next upside targets at $2,600 and $2,650.
"It's all fairly quiet. The move started in London late last night...charts are pointing up while stocks continue to fall," one said.
Others agreed that the market was waking up to the fact that copper is fundamentally as well as technically strong.
"It was good close last night. The market is very short and metal is still going out of warehouses," one senior trader said.
Copper stocks held in LME warehouses stand at 127,525 tonnes, well down on a recent peak of 222,500 seen in February.
The lack of available stock has seen backwardations flare.
Copper's cash to three months spread is moving towards a $100 backwardation, compared with $63 earlier this week.

A strike by workers at Canadian copper/nickel producer Inco Limited is also offering support. Its mining, smelting and refinery operation at Sudbury, Ontario has an annual production of around 100,000 tonnes of copper.
